title: Where we've got to on the slow CI
summary: A map of this conversation so far. We set out to get CI **under 10 minutes**, traced most of the time to a cold dependency cache, and chose remote caching over splitting the repo. Two things are still open: whether the cache can be trusted, and who owns it.

nodes.label: CI under 10 minutes
nodes.summary: The goal you opened with: pull requests currently wait about 38 minutes for a green build.
nodes.detail: You said the pain is context-switching: by the time CI finishes, people have moved on. Ten minutes was your number, chosen because it is short enough to wait for.

nodes.label: Cold dependency cache
nodes.summary: Every run reinstalls and rebuilds dependencies from scratch — roughly 21 of the 38 minutes.
nodes.detail:
Found by reading the timing breakdown you pasted from the last ten runs. The cache key includes the commit hash, so it never hits.

- install: ~6 min
- native rebuilds: ~15 min

nodes.label: Tests run serially
nodes.summary: The integration suite runs on one worker and takes about 11 minutes.
nodes.detail: The suite shares one database, which is why it was never parallelised. We agreed this is the second-biggest cost but not the first thing to fix.

nodes.label: Flaky retries
nodes.summary: About one run in six is retried, which inflates the average but not the typical run.
nodes.detail: You raised this; we set it aside as a separate problem.

nodes.label: Remote build cache
nodes.summary: Share build outputs between runs so unchanged work is downloaded instead of redone.
nodes.detail: My estimate was that this takes the dependency phase from ~21 minutes to ~3 on a typical pull request. It needs a storage bucket and a correct cache key.

nodes.label: Split the repository
nodes.summary: Give each service its own pipeline so a change only builds what it touches.
nodes.detail: You proposed this. We dropped it for now: it is weeks of work and the shared library changes in most pull requests anyway.

nodes.label: Shard the tests
nodes.summary: Run the integration suite on four workers, each with its own database.
nodes.detail: Would cut ~11 minutes to ~4. Depends on per-worker databases, which nobody has scoped yet.

nodes.label: Cache first, shard second
nodes.summary: We agreed to fix the cache key and add a remote cache this week, then look at sharding.
nodes.detail: Your reasoning: the cache is the bigger win and the smaller change. Expected result after step one is roughly **20 minutes**; the 10-minute target needs sharding too.

nodes.label: Can the cache be trusted?
nodes.summary: You are worried about a stale cache producing a green build that should be red.
nodes.detail: Not resolved. I suggested a nightly uncached run as a backstop; you wanted to think about it.

nodes.label: Who owns the cache?
nodes.summary: Nobody is on the hook for the bucket, its cost, or its eviction policy.
nodes.detail: You said you would raise it with the platform team. Not discussed further.
